title: Microbial Diversity
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 100L Microbiology curriculum covering the diversity and classification of microorganisms: bacteria, archaea, fungi, algae, protozoa and viruses, their general distinguishing features, habitats and classification schemes, as commonly taught alongside LASU's MCB101 Introductory Microbiology.

questions.question: Which taxonomic domain includes prokaryotic organisms that often live in extreme environments such as hot springs and salt lakes?
questions.correct_answer: Archaea
questions.explanation: Archaea are prokaryotes distinct from bacteria and are well known for including extremophiles that thrive in extreme heat, salinity or acidity.

questions.question: The three-domain system of classifying living organisms (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya) was proposed by which scientist?
questions.correct_answer: Carl Woese
questions.explanation: Carl Woese proposed the three-domain system in 1977 based on differences in ribosomal RNA sequences.

questions.question: Which of the following is the smallest and simplest of all microorganisms, unable to replicate outside a living host cell?
questions.correct_answer: Viruses
questions.explanation: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites lacking their own metabolic machinery, so they can only replicate inside a living host cell.

questions.question: Which group of microorganisms is characterized by a chitin-containing cell wall and absorptive (heterotrophic) nutrition?
questions.correct_answer: Fungi
questions.explanation: Fungi have cell walls made mainly of chitin and obtain nutrients by absorption after secreting extracellular digestive enzymes.

questions.question: Protozoa are best described as:
options: Single-celled eukaryotic organisms that are typically motile and heterotrophic
questions.correct_answer: Single-celled eukaryotic organisms that are typically motile and heterotrophic
questions.explanation: Protozoa are unicellular eukaryotes, most of which are motile (by flagella, cilia or pseudopodia) and obtain nutrients heterotrophically.

questions.question: Which structure distinguishes eukaryotic microorganisms from prokaryotic microorganisms?
options: The presence of a cell membrane
questions.correct_answer: A membrane-bound nucleus
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells possess a true, membrane-bound nucleus enclosing their genetic material, which prokaryotes lack.

questions.question: Algae are primarily distinguished from fungi by which feature?
options: Algae are photosynthetic and contain chlorophyll
questions.correct_answer: Algae are photosynthetic and contain chlorophyll
questions.explanation: Algae are photosynthetic eukaryotes containing chlorophyll and other pigments, unlike fungi which are non-photosynthetic and absorptive heterotrophs.

questions.question: Which binomial nomenclature rule is correctly applied in writing the name Escherichia coli?
options: Genus name capitalized, species name lowercase, both italicized
Both genus and species names fully capitalized
Genus and species both lowercase and underlined only
Species name capitalized before the genus name
questions.correct_answer: Genus name capitalized, species name lowercase, both italicized
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature convention requires the genus to be capitalized and the species epithet lowercase, with both italicized or underlined.

questions.question: Cyanobacteria were formerly called 'blue-green algae' but are correctly classified as:
questions.correct_answer: Photosynthetic bacteria (prokaryotes)
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria are prokaryotic, oxygen-evolving photosynthetic bacteria and are not true algae despite the historical name.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a virus's basic structure?
options: A nucleic acid core (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat called a capsid
A cell wall surrounding cytoplasm and a nucleus
A double membrane enclosing ribosomes only
questions.correct_answer: A nucleic acid core (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat called a capsid
questions.explanation: Viruses consist minimally of nucleic acid (either DNA or RNA, never both) surrounded by a protective protein capsid.

questions.question: Helminths (parasitic worms) are studied in microbiology mainly because:
options: They cause infectious disease and their eggs/larvae are identified by microscopy
They belong to the domain Bacteria
questions.correct_answer: They cause infectious disease and their eggs/larvae are identified by microscopy
questions.explanation: Although multicellular, helminths are included in microbiology/parasitology courses because they cause infections diagnosed via microscopic identification of eggs or larvae.

questions.question: Which of these organisms would be classified in the Kingdom Fungi?
questions.correct_answer: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast)
questions.explanation: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a unicellular yeast belonging to Kingdom Fungi, unlike the bacterium E. coli, the protozoan Plasmodium, or the alga Chlorella.

questions.question: Which feature is unique to archaea compared to bacteria?
options: Presence of chitin in the cell wall
questions.correct_answer: Cell walls that lack peptidoglycan
questions.explanation: Unlike bacteria, archaeal cell walls lack peptidoglycan; they may instead contain pseudopeptidoglycan or other polymers.

questions.question: Slime molds are unusual eukaryotic microorganisms because they:
options: Exhibit both amoeba-like and fungus-like stages in their life cycle
Have a rigid cell wall like plants at every stage
questions.correct_answer: Exhibit both amoeba-like and fungus-like stages in their life cycle
questions.explanation: Slime molds have a motile, amoeboid feeding stage and later form fungus-like fruiting bodies for spore dispersal, straddling protist and fungal characteristics.

questions.question: Which microbial group is most associated with causing malaria in humans?
questions.correct_answer: Protozoa (Apicomplexa)
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium species, protozoan parasites in the phylum Apicomplexa transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.question: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek is historically credited with:
options: First observing and describing microorganisms ('animalcules') using a simple microscope
Developing the germ theory of disease
questions.correct_answer: First observing and describing microorganisms ('animalcules') using a simple microscope
questions.explanation: Leeuwenhoek, using hand-crafted simple microscopes in the 17th century, was the first to observe and describe bacteria and protozoa, which he called 'animalcules'.

questions.question: Which of the following is a defining habitat characteristic of extremophilic archaea called halophiles?
options: Environments with very high salt concentration
questions.correct_answer: Environments with very high salt concentration
questions.explanation: Halophilic archaea are adapted to thrive in environments with extremely high salt concentrations, such as salt lakes and salterns.

questions.question: Which characteristic differentiates molds from yeasts within the Fungi kingdom?
options: Molds grow as multicellular filamentous hyphae, while yeasts are typically unicellular
Molds are prokaryotic, while yeasts are eukaryotic
Molds cannot reproduce, while yeasts reproduce by budding
Molds lack cell walls, while yeasts have cell walls
questions.correct_answer: Molds grow as multicellular filamentous hyphae, while yeasts are typically unicellular
questions.explanation: Molds form branching filaments called hyphae that make up a mycelium, whereas yeasts grow predominantly as single oval or round cells.

questions.question: Diatoms and dinoflagellates are examples of which microbial group?
questions.correct_answer: Algae
questions.explanation: Diatoms and dinoflagellates are photosynthetic microalgae that form major components of aquatic phytoplankton.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why viruses are often described as being 'at the edge of life'?
options: They display some characteristics of living things (genetic material, evolution) but cannot reproduce independently outside a host
They are entirely composed of inorganic chemicals
They have fully functional independent metabolism
questions.correct_answer: They display some characteristics of living things (genetic material, evolution) but cannot reproduce independently outside a host
questions.explanation: Viruses possess genetic material and can evolve, but lack independent metabolism and cannot reproduce without hijacking a host cell's machinery, placing them in a gray area between living and non-living.

questions.question: Prions, associated with diseases such as Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, are unique infectious agents because they:
options: Are composed entirely of misfolded protein with no nucleic acid
Contain only RNA and no protein
Are a type of fungal spore
questions.correct_answer: Are composed entirely of misfolded protein with no nucleic acid
questions.explanation: Prions are infectious misfolded protein particles that lack nucleic acid, distinguishing them from all other infectious agents.

questions.question: Which morphological shape describes cocci-shaped bacteria?
questions.correct_answer: Spherical
questions.explanation: Cocci are spherical or round-shaped bacteria, in contrast to rod-shaped bacilli or spiral-shaped spirilla.

questions.question: Lichens represent a symbiotic association typically between:
options: A fungus and a photosynthetic partner (alga or cyanobacterium)
questions.correct_answer: A fungus and a photosynthetic partner (alga or cyanobacterium)
questions.explanation: Lichens are a mutualistic symbiosis in which a fungal partner provides structure and protection while the photosynthetic alga or cyanobacterium supplies nutrients.

questions.question: Which of the following groups includes obligate intracellular bacteria such as Rickettsia and Chlamydia?
options: Bacteria with an obligate intracellular lifestyle similar in some ways to viruses
questions.correct_answer: Bacteria with an obligate intracellular lifestyle similar in some ways to viruses
questions.explanation: Rickettsia and Chlamydia are true bacteria but, unlike most bacteria, can only replicate inside host cells, which historically caused confusion with viruses.

questions.question: In the five-kingdom classification system proposed by Whittaker, bacteria are placed in which kingdom?
questions.correct_answer: Monera
questions.explanation: Whittaker's five-kingdom system placed all prokaryotes, including bacteria, in the kingdom Monera.

questions.question: Which of the following microbial groups reproduces by producing spores as a common survival/dispersal mechanism?
questions.correct_answer: Fungi
questions.explanation: Fungi commonly reproduce and disperse through the production of asexual or sexual spores, which are also used for surviving unfavorable conditions.

questions.question: What is the main ecological role played by decomposer microorganisms such as many fungi and bacteria?
options: Breaking down dead organic matter and recycling nutrients back into the environment
Causing all forms of disease in plants and animals
questions.correct_answer: Breaking down dead organic matter and recycling nutrients back into the environment
questions.explanation: Decomposer microbes degrade dead organic material, releasing nutrients such as carbon and nitrogen back into ecosystems for reuse.

questions.question: Bacteriophages are viruses that specifically infect:
questions.correct_answer: Bacteria
questions.explanation: Bacteriophages, often simply called phages, are viruses that specifically infect and replicate within bacterial cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a microorganism used as a source of single-cell protein for food/feed?
questions.correct_answer: Saccharomyces and Spirulina
questions.explanation: Yeast (Saccharomyces) and the cyanobacterium Spirulina are cultivated as sources of single-cell protein due to their high protein content and rapid growth.

questions.question: Which of the following criteria is NOT typically used to classify bacteria taxonomically?
options: The color of the growth medium in the bottle
questions.correct_answer: The color of the growth medium in the bottle
questions.explanation: Bacterial classification relies on morphology, Gram reaction, biochemical tests and molecular sequencing (e.g., 16S rRNA), not the incidental color of an unused growth medium container.

questions.question: Entamoeba histolytica, a protozoan parasite, is primarily responsible for which human disease?
questions.correct_answer: Amoebic dysentery
questions.explanation: Entamoeba histolytica is a protozoan that causes amoebic dysentery, characterized by invasive intestinal infection.

questions.question: Which statement about the size range of microorganisms is correct?
options: Viruses are generally smaller than bacteria, which are generally smaller than fungi and protozoa
Fungi are always smaller than viruses
All microorganisms are the same size regardless of type
questions.correct_answer: Viruses are generally smaller than bacteria, which are generally smaller than fungi and protozoa
questions.explanation: In general, viruses (nanometers) are smaller than bacteria (micrometers), which in turn are usually smaller than eukaryotic microbes like fungi and protozoa.
